records.title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
records.relevance_note: Outcome-based terminal benchmark with explicit verification design and failure taxonomy.
records.reason_included: Provides concrete benchmark construction, grading, audit, cost, and multi-run details.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Each task is defined by an instruction, Docker image, tests, example solution, and time limit; grading checks final container state rather than agent commands or console output.
Terminal-Bench 2.0 runs each supported agent-model configuration at least five times, yielding 32,155 total trials.
The benchmark publishes an explicit failure taxonomy that includes premature termination, no or irrelevant verification, and reasoning-action mismatch.

claim_locations.locator: Appendix C taxonomy, lines 1037-1089; taxonomy summary lines 672-679

records.title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
records.relevance_note: Primary source on continuous task refresh and decontaminated SWE evaluation.
records.reason_included: Directly addresses freshness, contamination, and automated benchmark construction.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper frames static interactive SWE benchmarks as becoming outdated quickly because contamination rises as models improve.
Its pipeline continuously extracts real-world interactive Python SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories and yields more than 21,000 tasks.
Fresh tasks collected with the same pipeline are used to build a contamination-free benchmark, and some models score lower there than on SWE-bench Verified.

records.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
records.relevance_note: Standardized multi-benchmark harness with cost, trace, and scaffold-level methodology.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete infrastructure, scale, cost, and auditability details for agent evaluation.

claim_snippets.claim_text: HAL standardizes agent evaluation with a harness that orchestrates parallel runs across hundreds of VMs, reducing runtime from weeks to hours while avoiding common implementation bugs.
The paper validates the harness with 21,730 agent rollouts across 9 models and 9 benchmarks at about $40,000 total cost.
LLM-aided log inspection surfaced benchmark-searching behavior and unintended credit-card misuse, and the release includes 2.5B tokens of agent logs.

records.title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
records.relevance_note: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability is a paper source with details on multi dimensional metrics, multi run reliability relevant to evals benchmarking.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on eval design, observability, cost budget.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The study replaces single-score evaluation with twelve reliability metrics spanning consistency, robustness, predictability, and safety.
Because grading errors were identified in tau-bench, the authors restrict analysis to 26 clean tasks and show that predictability and safety improve on the cleaned subset.
For reproducibility, the study uses deterministic generation settings, logged API calls via Weave, cached prompt perturbations, retries, and explicit timeout policies.

records.title: Introducing Bloom: an open source tool for automated behavioral evaluations
records.relevance_note: Introducing Bloom: an open source tool for automated behavioral evaluations is a engineering writeup source with details on automated eval generation, seeded reproducibility relevant to evals benchmarking.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on eval design, observability.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Bloom runs a four-stage automated pipeline: understanding, ideation, rollout, and judgment, turning a behavior description plus seed configuration into a complete evaluation suite.
Bloom-generated evals differ on each run while preserving the target behavior, and Anthropic states that suite metrics should always be cited together with the evaluation seed.
On a human-judge calibration check across 40 transcripts, Claude Opus 4.1 had the strongest correlation with human labels at 0.86.

A changelog records that an improved BrowseComp cheating-detection pipeline flagged additional unintended solutions, lowering previously reported scores without fully rerunning the evaluation.

ProtocolQA was converted from multiple-choice to open-ended short answer, and some evaluations were run without browsing specifically to avoid contamination.

records.title: MALT: A Dataset of Natural and Prompted Behaviors That Threaten Eval Integrity
records.exception_reason: Foundational source immediately before the primary window on monitor validation, heldout transcript release, and eval-integrity failure preservation.
records.relevance_note: MALT: A Dataset of Natural and Prompted Behaviors That Threaten Eval Integrity is a engineering writeup source with details on monitor ground truth dataset, heldout public split relevant to observability audit.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on observability, eval design.

claim_snippets.claim_text: MALT releases 10,919 agent transcripts over 403 tasks and 21 models, with 2,690 runs manually reviewed and all monitor results reported on the fully reviewed subset.
The public release is restricted to already-public tasks to preserve a heldout set and reduce benchmark contamination.

Best prompted monitors reach AUROCs of 0.96 for reward hacking and 0.91 for sandbagging, but the writeup cautions that transcript-only monitoring should not be relied on for subtle or realistic sandbagging.

records.title: Measuring Agents in Production
records.relevance_note: Empirical source on how deployed agent teams evaluate when public benchmarks do not fit.
records.reason_included: Anchors offline methodology against real production evaluation practice and online testing.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Among deployed agents in the study, 74% rely primarily on human-in-the-loop evaluation and 52% use LLM-as-a-judge.

Because public benchmarks are often not applicable to bespoke production tasks, 25% of teams build custom benchmarks and 75% rely on online tests such as A/B testing or direct expert or user feedback.
The study reports that production teams deliberately constrain autonomy, with 68% of agents taking at most ten steps before human intervention.

records.title: Efficient Benchmarking of AI Agents
records.relevance_note: Efficient Benchmarking of AI Agents is a paper source with details on mid range task selection, ranking over score prediction relevant to evals benchmarking.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on eval design, cost budget.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Across eight agent benchmarks, 33 scaffolds, and 70-plus model configurations, absolute score prediction degrades under scaffold and temporal shift while rank-order prediction remains stable.
A simple protocol that keeps tasks with intermediate historical pass rates of 30% to 70% cuts task count by 44% to 70% while preserving rank fidelity.
The paper argues that many practical benchmark uses are ranking problems, so a reduced suite can be justified even when calibrated score prediction collapses.

records.title: Establishing Best Practices in Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
records.relevance_note: Primary benchmark-methodology paper centered on task setup and reward-design failures.
records.reason_included: Explicitly quantifies benchmark overestimation and proposes a checklist for benchmark construction.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper argues that many agentic benchmarks suffer from task-setup or reward-design flaws, with examples including insufficient test cases in SWE-bench-Verified and empty responses counted as success in tau-bench.
The authors state that such flaws can over- or underestimate agent performance by up to 100% in relative terms.
Applying their Agentic Benchmark Checklist to CVE-Bench reduces measured overestimation by 33%.

rejections.rejection_reason: Public writeup is product-facing and does not expose enough stable source-local detail on holdouts, contamination control, or reproducible grading.
Leaderboard and product page rather than a primary methodology artifact.
Useful generic guidance, but not specific enough to agent-harness experimentation or online-offline alignment methodology.

records.title: What is LLM evaluation? A practical guide to evals, metrics, and regression testing
records.relevance_note: Provides clear operational definitions and pipelines for offline vs online agent evaluation, explicitly addressing dataset refresh cadence and holdout discipline.
records.reason_included: High-signal engineering perspective on preventing contamination and bridging the offline-online eval gap in production.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Offline evaluation acts as a safety net during development using curated datasets to catch regressions, while online evaluation monitors live traffic asynchronously to catch distribution shifts and novel queries.

Teams must regularly refresh evaluation datasets with new production cases while keeping a strict holdout set that is never optimized against to prevent data leakage and inflated generalization scores.

claim_locations.locator: Section: What is the difference between offline and online LLM evaluation?

records.title: Ablation Studies: The Operating System for Trustworthy AI Decisions
records.relevance_note: Directly addresses causal experiment design and ablation methodology for agent and RAG pipelines.
records.reason_included: Provides a concrete taxonomy of ablation failure modes (e.g., compute confounds, offline-online mismatch) critical for reliable agent experiment design.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Strong ablations must treat prompting/decoding, retrieval/reranking, data splits, and evaluation harnesses as first-class ablation targets, requiring negative controls and a declared tuning budget.

The biggest failure modes in ablation studies are compute confounds where capacity differences mask method gains, tuning asymmetry, data leakage, and offline-online mismatch where offline proxy gains vanish in live production.

claim_locations.locator: Section: Case studies and practitioner playbook

records.title: Cards Against Contamination: TCG-Bench for Difficulty-Scalable Multilingual LLM Reasoning
records.relevance_note: Introduces structural separation to solve benchmark contamination, keeping game implementation air-gapped from rules.
records.reason_included: Excellent example of strict holdout discipline and structural contamination prevention for LLM evaluations.

claim_snippets.claim_text: TCG-Bench prevents data contamination structurally by separating the public game engine mechanics from private card implementations, preventing models from memorizing test scenarios.
Evaluating models on a hidden holdout card set via API preserves evaluation integrity without requiring completely synthetic and unrealistic task designs.

records.title: A Blueprint for Self-Evolving Coding Agents in Vehicle Aerodynamic Drag Prediction
records.relevance_note: Industrial application demonstrating rigorous evaluation contracts for self-evolving coding agents, emphasizing split integrity and leakage prevention.
records.reason_included: Strong evidence for implementing strict evaluation contracts and holdout discipline in coding agent experiments.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Practical deployment of self-evolving agents requires a strict evaluation contract governing the executable pipeline to enforce split integrity, multi-seed robustness, and leakage prevention before any candidate is admitted.
Split policy guards enforce temporal and topological separation to prevent data leakage, ensuring that ranking performance remains decision-valid rather than artifact-driven.

records.reason_included: Highlights programmatic generation of benchmark state as a defense against data leakage in agent evaluations.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Context-Bench achieves a contamination-proof design by relying on programmatic SQL database generation, making the evaluation framework durable against training data memorization.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Training-time evaluation harnesses must treat optimization as an experiment repeated thousands of times under changing conditions, requiring strict holdout discipline.
A production agent is judged by its operational reality ('its Tuesday') rather than isolated demo success, necessitating evaluation metrics that reflect long-running state survival.

records.title: DigiData: Training and Evaluating General-Purpose Mobile Control Agents
records.exception_reason: Key early benchmark defining the methodological gap between offline proxy metrics (per-screenshot step-accuracy) and dynamic online evaluation (task success rate) for mobile agents.
records.relevance_note: Explicitly compares offline step-accuracy proxies with online dynamic task success rates in agent execution.
records.reason_included: Provides empirical evidence that dynamic online evaluations yield different signals than static offline accuracy for agent performance.

claim_snippets.claim_text: While dynamic evaluations provide a stronger signal around an agent's success in a trajectory, offline evaluation in the form of per-screenshot action matching remains a valuable proxy metric.

Online evaluations matter because static evaluation protocols often fail to capture compounding errors in multi-step execution, creating a gap between offline step-accuracy and online task success rate.
